claims.value: 21 April 1498: Gualtiero da Bascapè reports Leonardo promises to finish by September
claims.statement: A letter of the ducal secretary Gualtiero da Bascapè to Ludovico Sforza, April 1498, reports that the large room (camera grande) is being cleared of its planks and quotes 'Magistro Leonardo promete finirla per tuto septembre'. Day given as 21 April by one source, 20 April in the draft query; a second letter of the 23rd reports the room free of the boards.

background.text: The Sala delle Asse, is a large room in the Castello Sforzesco in Milan, the location of a painting in tempera on plaster by Leonardo da Vinci, dating from about 1498. Its walls and vaulted ceiling are decorated with "intertwining plants with fruits and monochromes of roots and rocks" and a canopy created by sixteen trees.

La Sala delle Asse è una sala che si trova al piano terra del torrione nord-orientale, detto anche del Falconiere, del Castello Sforzesco di Milano. Prende il nome dalle assi di legno che si ritiene un tempo rivestissero le pareti.

La Sala delle Asse, la salle de l'axe en italien, également appelée Pièce de la tour ou Pièce des lambris est une salle du château des Sforza dont le plafond a très probablement été décoré par Léonard de Vinci selon une commande de Ludovic le More.
